_open_questions: Maximum time-alignment delay: datasheet 0-17 ms vs 0-692 cm (mutually inconsistent), vs the demo software's 425 cm = 12.50 ms at 340 m/s. `delay.max_ms` stays null until a connected unit says. Nothing is blocked by this -- in-car TA rarely exceeds ~8 ms.

The odd-order 'Linkwitz' menu entries (6/18/30/42 dB/oct) are recorded in prose but NOT in `crossover_filters.types.LR`: a true LR alignment exists only at even orders, and their real phase behaviour is unmeasured. Measure before adding them to a search space.
The optical input accepts PCM up to 96 kHz / 24 bit per the datasheet; sample-rate conversion to the 48 kHz core rate is INFERRED, not vendor-confirmed.
STRUCTURAL, not a question: the matrix per-cell level has no field token in the ledger vocabulary, so it is stored as a descriptive key only and cannot be proposed as a normal field edit.

channel_gain.note: Attenuation only -- no positive gain, so all headroom management is downward and a quiet channel cannot be trimmed up. Separate master level 0...-59 dB.

crossover_filters.slope_range_note: The MENU offers Bessel, Butterworth and Linkwitz each at 6/12/18/24/30/36/42/48 dB/oct (vendor datasheet, 'TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS'). LR is recorded here at EVEN orders only, and that is a deliberate narrowing, not a transcription error: a true Linkwitz-Riley alignment exists only at even orders, so the odd-order LR entries are vendor menu labelling whose actual phase behaviour nobody has measured. Feeding them to a search would put filters we cannot model into the space the search picks a winner from -- the same shape as the Helix CHEBYSHEV family, which is excluded for the same reason. If the odd-order LR entries are ever measured on hardware, add them back with the measurement beside them.

delay.max_ms_note: UNRESOLVED, and null rather than a guess. The datasheet states 0-17 ms AND 0-692 cm, which contradict each other (692 cm at the datasheet's own implied 350 m/s is 19.8 ms). The PC software (DEMO build, no unit connected) showed a 425 cm maximum = exactly 12.50 ms at 340 m/s, and a demo build may not expose a connected unit's real limits. Practical impact is near zero -- in-car time alignment rarely exceeds ~8 ms -- so nothing is blocked by leaving it open, while a plausible bound written here becomes a limit code enforces and nobody re-questions.
delay.speed_of_sound_note: The UI converts ms <-> cm internally and TWO constants are implied by different vendor sources: the datasheet step pairs (0.08 ms = 2.8 cm, 0.02 ms = 0.7 cm) imply 350 m/s, while the software's 425 cm / 12.5 ms limit implies 340 m/s. Never hand-convert: propose delay in ms and let the app derive centimetres.
delay.step_ms_note: 0.021 ms is one sample at 48 kHz; the datasheet's own 'Time Alignment Fine Set: 0.02 ms' is the same figure rounded. This is the second, independent witness for the 48 kHz processing rate.

dsp_profile.dsp_processing_rate_note: Derived, not vendor-stated. The datasheet gives only 'DIGITAL SIGNAL PROCESSOR (64 bit Clock speed: 295 MHz)'; that is the Analog Devices SigmaDSP ADAU145x core clock 294.912 MHz = 6144 x 48 kHz. Corroborated independently by the delay fine step being exactly 1/48000 s. Generalizable: any DSP quoting a ~295 MHz clock is an ADAU145x at 48 kHz.

groups.label: Output channels
groups.note: 6 amplified channels + 2 RCA pre-outs. There is no virtual/group tier on this model.

input_routing.input_processing: level (gain) only -- no per-input EQ or delay

matrix.per_cell_level_note: The mix level is set in EVERY matrix cell (input -> output), not once per input source, so there is no per-input processing row at all.

measurement_input.operational_note: Input selection follows the preset on this unit, so every preset used during measurement must have the same input selected. And because per-input level lives in the matrix cells, the measurement input's row must carry identical cell levels across the channels being compared -- an unequal cell level presents as a level error that looks acoustic.
measurement_input.rationale: Aux RCA works as a dedicated measurement input: the sweep bypasses the head unit, so measurements carry no OEM EQ, loudness or level-dependent processing.

dsp_profile.name: M6V4

parametric_eq.eq_transfer_note: No EQ file import. Filters move from REW with REW-EQ-CopyPaste-Assistant (github.com/IvanBakhmutov/REW-EQ-CopyPaste-Assistant), which types them into the MUSWAY window. A proposal must therefore be expressible as REW PK filters on the grid F=1 Hz / Q=0.01 / G=0.1 dB, within 31 bands per channel, and PK only -- this processor has no shelf and no all-pass band.

polarity.implementation: 0/180 degree switch only -- no continuous all-pass phase control

presets.note: The silent input reset trap (competition.md Pre-session #4): give every preset used during a session the same input, and check the input after every switch.

dsp_profile.variant_note: This entry describes the NON-512K unit (ADAU1452). The 512K variant is different silicon (ADAU1466) whose published DSP specification block is byte-identical, so the sheet cannot be used to infer one from the other. A tuner who names the variant when starting a project ('M6V4 (no 512K)') will not match this entry by name -- `find_bundled` is exact by design.
